title: The Industrial Revolution
summary: How steam, factories and railways changed work, cities and the world from the late 1700s.

steps.title: Before machines
sentences: Before the Industrial Revolution most people lived in villages and farmed.
Goods were made by hand in homes or small workshops.
Travel was as fast as a horse or a sailing ship.

steps.title: Steam power
sentences: In Britain in the 1700s, inventors improved the steam engine, and James Watt made it much more efficient.
Steam could drive machines in factories and pull trains on railways.
Cotton spinning and weaving machines made cloth far faster than hand work.

steps.title: Big changes
sentences: People moved from villages into growing cities to work in factories.
Many factories were crowded and unsafe, and children also worked, which led to new laws and trade unions.
Cities grew fast and also had pollution and poor housing for many years.

steps.title: A world connected
sentences: Railways and steamships brought distant places closer and made trade faster.
The changes spread to Europe, America, and later Asia, including India, where railways were built from the 1850s.
Today's world of machines, mass production and energy use began here.

facts: The first passenger railway in India ran from Bombay to Thane in 1853.
Burning coal for factories began to raise the amount of carbon dioxide in the air.
Many historians say this change was as big as the move from hunting to farming.

quiz.q: Which invention powered early factories and trains?
quiz.why: Improved steam engines drove machines and locomotives.
People moved to cities to work in factories.

quiz.q: When was the first passenger train in India?
quiz.why: The first passenger train ran from Bombay to Thane in 1853.
